name: Dimension-Five Daisy Host Chain
definition: Fix $P=\{p\}$, $R=\{a,b,c,e\}$, and $A=\{a,b\}$. Use the nested down-sets $\mathcal W_{12}=\langle ab,ce\rangle$, $\mathcal W_{14}=\langle ab,ae,ce\rangle$, and $\mathcal W_{16}=\langle ab,ae,be,ce\rangle$, then delete the distinguished antipodal pair from $2^P\times\mathcal W_j$.
properties: The three single-root factors have seven, eight, and nine vertices, while $A$ and its complement remain maximal. Their punctured products are pairwise nonisomorphic ample daisy obstructions of orders 12, 14, and 16, all of isometric dimension five. Each host step adds one factor vertex and hence two obstruction vertices.
